name: CACHE
one_line: Light CORRIE-derived shell with a drawcord collar under a lid; three removable roll-top modules and two hook-on side pods; the frame-zone SWAP slab carries the sleep kit and becomes the wipeable meat liner under IM1-IM3 on a pack-out.
pack_mass_note: 3943 - 892.1 + 991.0 (CORRIE B.2 counted by the same metric in cache.corrie_b2_system(): body group, roll-top hardware, keeper loops, IMP-1/2/4/8, haul wraps, fly; IMP-6/IMP-3/IMP-5 and the fixed interface are out on both sides)
volume_note: cloth-sim closed volume of the fill case, mean of 15/19/23 in (CORRIE rev B shell, 85.2 L design number by the same R-01 basis as CORRIE); modules hold 20.3 + 17.2 + 6.6 L inside it; the LID module (2.7 L) and the pods ride outside and are not counted
cg_note: mass-weighted CG y incl. the lid module (1.08 kg) and the optics pod with an 85 mm spotter (1.99 kg), coarse h 40 mm, all 6 cases converged; read +<=4 mm for the contact-rounding bias
features: SWAP slab module: sleep kit in camp, emptied and re-used as the wipeable meat liner under IM1-IM3
IM1-IM3 double as internal compression: they cinch the modules flat against the frame on small loads
Modules slide out through CORRIE's #10 horseshoe door like drawers (CAMP), KILL module at the sill
Drawcord collar + LID module (2.7 L) replace the roll-top; LID front straps are the top compression
Optics pod (85 mm spotter) and tripod kit hook on with G-hooks to the old wing loops; leave them home
SP snack pocket on the right shoulder strap: snacks reachable pack-on on every belt size
Quiet: modules close by roll + G-hook (no buckle clack), no hook-and-loop, coil zips only
Frame interface, IM straps, under-straps, hood, guys, hinge eyes, fly pocket: unchanged from CORRIE
risks: Heavier than CORRIE B.2 by 98.9 g as counted (the 3 modules are 137.2 g); lighter only if the hunter leaves stuff sacks home
Shell = CORRIE rev B shell: the cloth sim is effectively a re-run, not a new body; 15 in meat CG margin is 7.9 mm (>= 3.9 mm with the rounding bias)
No roll-top: the cinched collar is not waterproof; relies on the lid, the fly and the dry-bag modules
Module walls and corners cost usable volume (fill efficiency 0.90 -> 0.86 ASSUMPTION)
Silpoly modules on bone ends / brush: no abrasion data; SWAP frame face + floor in 70D (test MOD-2)
Sheep loadout: GPS (S-L belts) and the 2nd bottle still miss pack-on access; rain shell rides in the bag
Kill-site sequencing: the sleep kit has to go somewhere while the slab becomes the liner (aft column)
Snack pocket and lid straps were not drawn in every render; the pod cinch straps are drawn simplified
